status: DRAFT - NOT PUBLISHED. REVIEW owns placement and publication.
component: Third-party components compiled into the Windows media playback library libmpv-2.dll

premise_correction.task_premise: libmpv-2.dll is a GPL build; produce GPL compliance materials for shipped releases 0.8.0+992 and 0.8.0+993.
premise_correction.finding: The premise does not hold. The shipped DLL was built with -Dgpl=false and is LGPLv2.1-or-later.
premise_correction.authority: The meson configure line embedded in the shipped binary itself; see evidence/mpv-meson-configure-line.txt and LICENCE-DETERMINATION.md.
premise_correction.effect: No GPL obligation arises from libmpv for any shipped build. An LGPL obligation does arise, for all builds, and is currently unmet.

applies_to.linkage: mpv, FFmpeg and their dependencies are statically compiled into the DLL; the app dynamically loads the DLL
applies_to.identical_across_releases: Byte-identical in all 19 sampled Windows builds, 0.7.2+980 through 0.8.1+1001

derivation.method: Parsed the two configure lines recovered from the shipped binary itself: FFmpeg's configuration string and mpv's meson command line. Corroborated per component against distinctive data strings in the same binary.
derivation.explicitly_not_used: The build repository's packages/ directory. It catalogues 100+ package definitions including GPL-only ones (libdvdnav, libdvdread, x264, x265, avisynth-headers, libbluray) and others plainly not in this artefact (aom, libvpx, lame, opus, flac, curl, luajit). Membership of that directory is not evidence of presence in the binary.
derivation.flag_order_resolution: The FFmpeg configure line contains both --enable-libmfx and, later, --disable-libmfx. FFmpeg's configure applies flags in order, so the later flag wins and libmfx is NOT enabled. Intel hardware support in this build comes from libvpl (oneVPL) instead. --disable-libuavs3d likewise excludes libuavs3d.
derivation.method_limits: This build uses -Db_lto=true, -Wl,--gc-sections, --prefer-static and --enable-stripping. Internal symbol names do not survive; only data strings do. Presence of a distinctive data string is good evidence a component is in. Absence of a symbol name is NOT evidence a component is out. Absence of a data string is evidence only where a comparable control string is present. Confidence values below reflect this.

licence_election.version3_rationale: mbedtls is Apache-2.0, incompatible with GPLv2 but compatible with the v3 family. The version3 election is what makes this component set coherent.

mpv_components.name: mujs
mpv_components.version_bound_basis: Build date of this artefact is on or about 2023-09-24, from its own 'libjpeg-turbo version 3.0.1 (build 20230924)' string. MuJS 1.3.4 (a76d157bdaa9) is dated 2023-11-21, after the build, so 1.3.3 is the highest tag that could be present.
mpv_components.licence_evidence: COPYING at tag 1.3.3 is the ISC Licence, 'Copyright (c) 2013-2020 Artifex Software, Inc.', in both ccxvii/mujs and ArtifexSoftware/mujs. Every tag from 1.0.0 through 1.3.3 was checked and is likewise ISC, so an untagged snapshot between them does not change the answer.
mpv_components.note: SUPERSEDES an earlier 'FLAG AS AN OPEN LEGAL QUESTION / possibly AGPL-3.0' classification, which rested on an unbounded claim about modern MuJS and was not pinned to this artefact. The bound above cannot move with future upstream relicensing. Not claimed here: that MuJS is ISC-only as a project today - Artifex dual-licenses commercially, and that is an open legal question separate from this artefact.

mpv_components.name: libpng

mpv_components.name: mingw-w64 runtime
mpv_components.note: Toolchain runtime linked into the DLL. Named for completeness; commonly treated as a system/toolchain library rather than a redistributed component. Whether it belongs in the notice is an open question.

unresolved.item: Build-definition commit does not match the artefact
unresolved.detail: packages/mpv.cmake at media-kit/libmpv-win32-video-build 0837d6b2eb declares -Dlua=enabled -Dopenal=enabled -Dvulkan=enabled -Dlibplacebo=enabled and contains no -Dgpl flag. The shipped binary says the opposite on all four and adds -Dgpl=false. That commit therefore did not produce this artefact, or overrides were applied outside the file.
unresolved.impact: Blocks citing a build definition in the Corresponding Source offer. Does not affect the licence determination, which rests on the binary.
unresolved.needed: Identify the commit or workflow run that produced release 2023-09-24, or reproduce the build and compare.

unresolved.item: MuJS licence arm - RESOLVED 2026-08-08, retained so it is not re-opened
unresolved.detail: This entry previously read: 'JavaScript support is enabled and MuJS is present, but the MuJS version is not recoverable from the binary and MuJS changed from ISC to AGPL-3.0.' That is withdrawn. The version does not need to be read from the build definition, because it can be bounded by date: this artefact's own 'libjpeg-turbo version 3.0.1 (build 20230924)' string puts the build on or about 2023-09-24, and MuJS 1.3.4 is dated 2023-11-21, so 1.3.3 (2023-01-10) is the highest tag that could be present. Every tag from 1.0.0 through 1.3.3 is ISC. See the mujs component entry above for the full basis.
unresolved.impact: None. libmpv does not contain an AGPL component, and it does not depend on the build-definition gap.
unresolved.needed: Nothing for this artefact. Separately, and not blocking: a legal review may want a view on Artifex's commercial dual-licensing of MuJS as a project today.

unresolved.detail: Not named on the recovered mpv meson line and not gpl-gated, so autodetection could have enabled it. The only 'bluray' string in the binary is 'pcm_bluray', which is an FFmpeg codec name and not libbluray.
unresolved.impact: Minor. Affects completeness of the component list.

counts.carrying_source_obligation_note: Corrected 2026-08-08: 'mujs (if AGPL)' was removed from this list. MuJS is bounded to <= 1.3.3, which is ISC, so it is credit-required and carries no source obligation. See the mujs component entry and the resolved MuJS open_question.
counts.licence_texts_completeness_note: Derived and recorded 2026-08-14 by S&C (the 'state the number, and if zero say so explicitly' item). Every libmpv component carrying a source/licence-text obligation has its licence document held: libfribidi (LGPL-2.1-or-later) and libsoxr (LGPL-2.1-or-later) have their COPYING captured under docs/release/evidence/license-sources/ and in the FFmpeg corresponding-source HOLDING; uchardet is tri-licensed (MPL-1.1 OR GPL-2.0-or-later OR LGPL-2.1-or-later) and is elected LGPL-2.1-or-later per docs/DECISIONS.md (2026-08-09 owner-decision on the five licence questions), so the 'supply a copy of this License' limb is satisfied by the LGPL-2.1 document already held via libfribidi/libsoxr. Missing set therefore = 0. Full derivation: docs/security/findings/FFMPEG_LIBMPV_LICENCE_TEXTS_COMPLETENESS_2026-08-14.md (workspace).
